counts.explanation: npm audit totals count affected package entries, including propagated parent findings. Distinct GHSA totals deduplicate advisory URLs; one GHSA can have multiple npm source IDs or ranges (notably separate undici major lines). These are not counts of independently demonstrated exploitable vulnerabilities.

acceptance.note: Independent final review of 23850ea792ea767de8ea0f17ac9175c64aef7209 found no PR-specific code blocker; its documentation correction is recorded here. Maintainer merge/scope disposition remains pending. EXA-70 tracks unresolved Vite work and EXA-66 retains its runtime hold. Production-only audit excludes shipped Electron; local/CI validation does not establish installed NSIS/Store acceptance.

dependencyChainMethod: Resolved package-lock v3 dependency, optionalDependency, peerDependency and root devDependency edges using nested node_modules resolution. Each package evidence node lists every acyclic root-to-node dependency chain; cyclic peer back-edges are excluded to avoid infinite paths. Exact parent constraints and dependency kinds are retained. Optional installation is platform-dependent; lock presence is recorded without asserting execution.

applicabilityProfiles.@xmldom/xmldom: Dev-only builder plist XML parsing/serialization graph. Injection and resource-exhaustion behavior depends on malformed/untrusted XML or constructed nodes. No packaged production path is present in this lock. Compatible 0.8.15 repair is applied, without relying on a trust or platform exception.
applicabilityProfiles.app-builder-lib: Linux AppImage generated-runtime library-search-path issue. This checkout configures Windows NSIS and validation uses --win --dir; neither produces the affected AppImage runtime. Updated app-builder-lib nonetheless removes the vulnerable version. This is not installed NSIS or Store acceptance.
applicabilityProfiles.baseline-browser-mapping: Dev-only Babel/browserslist target resolution; invalid input can terminate the process. Updated within its existing parent range, so no input-trust exception is required.
applicabilityProfiles.browserslist: Dev-only Babel compilation-target queries/custom stats can cause unbounded cache growth or crash/prototype writes. Compatible browserslist update is applied; not a packaged application dependency.
applicabilityProfiles.builder-util-runtime: Build/publish/download HTTP utility can leak PRIVATE-TOKEN or mixed-case Authorization on cross-origin redirects. It is dev-only in this lock and not part of the application production dependency tree. No assumption of credential absence is needed for disposition: the compatible builder update replaces the affected utility.
applicabilityProfiles.electron: Unchanged shipped Electron 43.1.0 matches this advisory range. Current renderer/window hardening is preserved, but no exploitability exception or release approval is granted. Runtime remediation, embedded Node/Chromium validation and the independent Chromium hold remain EXA-66 work.
applicabilityProfiles.GHSA-9qh4-3jw8-366w: Electron webview/worker integration restriction bypass. Renderer isolation and current window safeguards are preserved; no proof of complete inapplicability was attempted. The shipped Electron 43.1.0 remains vulnerable by version and is owned by the separate EXA-66 runtime review.
applicabilityProfiles.GHSA-h3v5-h239-pg29: Explicitly concerns macOS off-screen rendering and GPU-supplied frame geometry. Windows is the current target. The vulnerable Electron version is nevertheless unchanged and its runtime security hold remains with EXA-66; this individual platform observation does not clear that hold.
applicabilityProfiles.GHSA-jr5w-w6x2-84p9: Shipped Electron certificate-trust mitigation, distinct from npm package-only production audit and host Node. No configuration-based inapplicability is claimed; remains under the EXA-66 runtime/Chromium hold.
applicabilityProfiles.esbuild: esbuild serve API CORS/source disclosure. Inspected project scripts and installed electron-vite/Vite use build/transform/context and did not establish an esbuild serve endpoint. The vulnerable esbuild package remains at 0.21.5 and is retained as unresolved rather than accepted risk. Vite separately runs its own dev server, which has distinct advisories. Patched esbuild >=0.25.0 does not satisfy electron-vite ^0.21.5 or Vite ^0.21.3.
applicabilityProfiles.http-cache-semantics: Build-only old @electron/get -> got -> cacheable-request graph. The alleged cross-user shared-cache/max-stale Bug Pocket exploit was not demonstrated. The captured compatible update 4.2.0 -> 4.3.0 leaves the published <=4.2.0 range and removes this entry from the dated after audit. The official advisory lists no patched version; the upstream owner disputes the report. Audit-range removal is not evidence of a verified code-level security fix. No security exception or application exploit claim is made.
applicabilityProfiles.js-yaml: Build-tool YAML config parser can exhaust CPU on malicious YAML merge/omap constructs. Repository config uses package.json, but this is a parser repair rather than a configuration exception.
applicabilityProfiles.nanoid: Dev-only PostCSS graph; affected custom generator behavior can loop indefinitely with zero size. Compatible patched 3.x version is locked; no production application API is inferred from this dev dependency.
applicabilityProfiles.postcss: Dev-only Vite CSS build processing; crafted sourceMappingURL with from unset can read arbitrary source maps. Compatible patched PostCSS 8.x version is locked; build-input trust is not used as an exception.
applicabilityProfiles.source-map-js: Dev-only PostCSS source-map handling; malformed indexed map offsets can exhaust the event loop. Patched compatible 1.2.2 is locked.
applicabilityProfiles.tar: Dev-only builder packaging and native node-gyp install/rebuild archive path; a crafted long-path archive with member selection can trigger uncatchable recursion. Patched compatible 7.5.22 is locked; native rebuilding remains enabled.
applicabilityProfiles.undici: Build/install-time @electron/get optional HTTP client and node-gyp HTTP client, on separate 7.x and 6.x branches. Advisory-specific network/cache/retry/WebSocket/EventSource/TLS prerequisites differ; no blanket inapplicability is asserted. Both supported parent ranges now resolve to patched releases and the after audit reports no undici finding. Node/Electron built-in fetch is a separate runtime, not repaired by this lock update.
applicabilityProfiles.vite: Vite development-server optimized-dependency source-map traversal. Official advisory requires an exposed dev server and predictable sensitive .map files. Repository electron.vite.config.ts has no host override; CI builds and packaged app smoke do not launch the Vite dev server. Developer invocation can change exposure, so this remains pending a coordinated Vite/electron-vite migration.
applicabilityProfiles.GHSA-587h-7wmj-h5pm: Windows launch-editor fs.existsSync path-check bypass removes a filesystem-existence prerequisite and combines with percent escaping to permit command injection. Bundled vulnerable editor middleware remains in Vite 5.4.21. Packaged static renderer and CI build do not invoke the editor endpoint, but Windows developer use remains unresolved.
applicabilityProfiles.GHSA-698v-4r3x-3vcv: Windows bundled launch-editor argument escaping can permit command injection with crafted percent-containing inputs and attacker-controlled environment/NTFS conditions. Developer middleware risk remains; no hostile-input acceptance or general inapplicability is claimed. Fix must replace bundled Vite code through a coordinated major migration.
applicabilityProfiles.GHSA-9jrq-w75r-8gcw: Requires custom middleware passing an unchanged browser URL to transformIndexHtml, inline module script and sensitive values/actions. Inspected repository config uses the standard renderer SPA and no such custom middleware. This specific prerequisite was not found, but the Vite version remains affected and requires the broader migration; no package-wide exception inferred.
applicabilityProfiles.GHSA-fx2h-pf6j-xcff: Windows/NTFS development-server fs.deny bypass using ADS or 8.3 paths. Official advisory requires network-exposed dev-server use and sensitive files inside the allow roots. Current config has no host override; CI build and packaged app serve static output rather than a Vite dev server. This does not waive possible developer exposure; pending migration.
applicabilityProfiles.GHSA-r825-w8mm-5pxw: Bundled launch-editor can misinterpret paths as editor CLI flags. Applicability depends on attacker-created filesystem entries, selected editor and direct/middleware/WSL path conditions described by the advisory. Those developer configurations were not exhaustively tested; remain pending migration rather than declaring all Windows uses safe.
applicabilityProfiles.GHSA-rq7h-c2jc-7f22: Official advisory requires a non-Windows Vite dev server plus network exposure, a matching root-relative imported/system path and a readable file outside deny rules. It excludes this Windows CI/smoke platform. Non-Windows developer use was not accepted or tested; retained in migration scope.
applicabilityProfiles.GHSA-v6wh-96g9-6wx3: Windows development-server bundled launch-editor middleware can disclose an NTLMv2 hash through a UNC path. A malicious website requesting the known running middleware is a documented prerequisite; loopback binding does not by itself establish inapplicability. Installed Vite 5.4.21 registers /__open-in-editor and bundles the editor code, so a separate launch-editor override would not patch it. No packaged Vite server is used; developer risk remains pending migration.

evidenceLookup: Each advisory references packageEvidence by package name. Its per-snapshot node IDs index dependencyGraphs.before/after.nodes. Each chain is an ordered array of edge IDs indexing that snapshot's edges; edge from/to IDs identify exact lock paths and versions. Source-range affected node IDs use the same snapshot tables. Applicability, proposed scope and range validation are shared by explicit profile/disposition keys to avoid repeated prose. Raw audits retain original CVSS/CWE metadata.
